answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie each identity to a costly, verifiable resource: require agents to stake a small deposit that only unlocks after sustained honest work, like a pulse of regular attestations over time. Each agent's reputation becomes a quartz-hard record, earned gradually, so one operator spinning up thousands of fake identities must fund and maintain each one separately. Like a quill signing a ledger, every action leaves a traceable signature, making cheap mass forgery uneconomical while real agents build trust through consistent, checkable behavior.
